Jordan (customer): Getting a 401 when hitting POST /v1/generate from our Android app (WebView). No request id shown in app logs or UI. Error screen only says "unauthorized". Can you help?

Aisha: Sorry you're hitting that. Quick Qs: what app build and exact time (UTC +/- 2m)? Also, can you capture a network trace or HAR from the device? That will usually contain the edge request headers we need.

Jordan (customer): Build v3.2.1, happened at 2025-11-03 14:12:08 UTC. I'm not a dev — how do I get a HAR from Android WebView?

Liam: Two non-dev friendly ways: 1) If you can connect device to a laptop: enable remote debug in the WebView and use Chrome -> chrome://inspect -> inspect -> Network tab -> reproduce -> right-click -> Save as HAR. 2) If you can't USB-debug, install a proxy (e.g., Charles/Proxyman) on the device and record the session, then export the session. Either one is fine.

Liam: What we need from the HAR / network capture (minimal):
- Timestamp window (you already gave it, perfect)
- The POST request headers for the failing call. Look for any header named like `x-request-id`, `x-rw-req`, `x-session`, or anything with `req`/`correlator`
- The Host header (edge hostname) or full request URL
- Full response status code and body (copy exact message)

Aisha: If the customer can't get a HAR, ask them to video the chrome inspector network panel or take screenshots of the request headers. Screenshots are OK. If they can run a curl, share this snippet (they can redact tokens):

Liam: ```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: <copy-if-you-see-it>" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-small","input":"test"}'
```

Jordan (customer): I can do the chrome://inspect route. I captured a HAR but I only see `x-session: 62d4...` on the request, no x-request-id. The Host header is `edge-us-03.rw-inference.com`. Response body is `{\"error\":\"unauthorized\",\"code\":401}`.

Raj: x-session is useful, include the full value. Our edge sometimes maps session -> correlator internally. Also include the exact timestamp and the edge host you pasted. We'll search logs for that host + time window + session value.

Aisha: If you can, upload the HAR and the short video/screenshots to the support ticket. If the customer can run the SDK or app with debug logs enabled, ask them to enable and paste any lines that mention `reqref`, `correlator`, or `traceid`. For JS/Node SDK: set `client.logLevel = 'debug'`. For mobile SDKs, enable verbose / debug logging in the app.

Liam: If they prefer a one-click repro bundle: from Console -> Sessions -> find the user session -> Copy debug bundle and attach that token to the ticket. That bundle contains server-side spans and the debug_token we can resolve. We can also generate a debug bundle on our side if you supply the HAR + session value + time window.

Jordan (customer): I can't access Console. I attached the HAR and a short video. Also ran the curl snippet; it returns 401 too. I redacted the Authorization header.

console-bot: debug bundle generated: token=dbg_8c2f1a — Aisha, you can ask the customer to add this token to the ticket or we can upload on their behalf if they consent.

Raj: Perfect. Next steps for us: 1) We'll correlate edge host `edge-us-03.rw-inference.com`, timestamp 2025-11-03 14:12:08 UTC, and `x-session: 62d4...` in our logs. 2) If we need deeper traces we'll request the debug bundle from the ticket (token above) or ask customer to upload. 3) If we find a mapped request id / trace id we'll paste it back here with the log excerpt.

Aisha: Thanks Jordan — once you confirm you've attached the HAR + video and (if ok) the debug token, we'll escalate to infra with the details. :thumbsup:
